ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each director, officer, shareholder, and UBO against OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, and Public Safety Canada's aggregated sanctions and high-risk listings. PEP detection and enhanced due diligence are required under FINTRAC guidance issued under the PCMLTFA and the Alberta Corporate Registry's know-your-corporate-client requirements. Positive hits require refusal, Suspicious Transaction Report filing where applicable, and escalation to legal counsel.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official filing language is English, with French permitted as an official-language alternative; all names must be entered in Latin script. An Alberta unlimited liability corporation must include the legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC' in its corporate name. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. Names must be distinguishable from all existing reserved and registered names in the Alberta Corporate Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Director of Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) within 30 days of the refusal notice, attaching the original Name Search Report, the stated grounds of refusal, and evidence of distinctiveness, consent, or distinguishing elements. If refusal is administratively upheld, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the applicable name provisions of the Business Corporations Act. An existing name reservation may be renewed if applied for before expiry; the initial name search report or reservation is valid for 90 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally permissible as the registered office of an Alberta ULC if it is a real street address in Alberta, accepts service during normal business hours, and is administered by a registered agent. For ISIC 5820 / Steam-console digital publishing, no physical storefront is required; however, Canada Revenue Agency and the Alberta Corporate Registry may assess whether substantive management and decision-making actually occur in Alberta for tax residency and pass-through eligibility purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 4% probability during the first 12 months) for a low-risk digital publisher holding no statutory license; unannounced inspections are rare in the ordinary course, but credible non-compliance indicators may trigger a FINTRAC, CRA, or corporate registry site inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), ss. 6-16 (incorporation mechanics), s. 101 (registered office), s. 102 (corporate records); Alberta Companies Act, RSA 2000, c C-21 (unlimited liability share structure); Income Tax Act (Canada), s. 136.3 (ULC status recognition); Alta Reg 239/2000 (Business Corporations Act Regulation)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta / Alberta Registries, 11th Floor, 10220-103 Street NW, Edmonton, AB T5J 4N7, Canada
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) and Certificate of Incorporation issued through the Alberta Corporate Registry online incorporation portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital in Alberta; a nominal CAD 1.00 subscription consideration is acceptable. No escrow account or capital trust deposit is required. The Articles may authorize a single class of Common Shares and the Board may allot shares from treasury at any time, subject to the applicable solvency test requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED that the share subscriptions detailed in the Subscription Agreement are accepted, and the allotment and issuance of Common Shares to the Founding Shareholders is approved, effective upon receipt of consideration; RESOLVED that the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at Suite 800, 333 7th Avenue SW, Calgary, Alberta T2P 2Z1, Canada, where statutory records shall be maintained; RESOLVED that the following persons are appointed Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each with the usual authority and duties; RESOLVED that the Board authorizes management to open bank accounts, engage professional advisors, and execute all ancillary documents to give effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – NUANS Name Search Group (Service Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Name Reservation Request containing the proposed name and the mandatory legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'. The registry conducts a NUANS (Newly Updated Automated Name Search) screening for prohibited marks, corporate name conflicts, and trademark similarity. A NUANS report valid for 90 days is obtained; pay the prescribed search fee and retain the reservation confirmation or conflict listing for remediation.
required_dossiers: Brief business purpose narrative (ISIC 5820 software publishing)
NUANS Name Search Report and fee receipt (CAD 25.00)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged, file a Name Reservation Reply or select a revised distinctive element; a fresh NUANS search may be waived within 30 days if only the corporate designator changes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Online 'Incorporate Now' Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Form 1 Articles stating: (a) corporate name with ULC suffix; (b) unlimited liability class of shares with no authorized maximum; (c) share transfer restrictions, if any; (d) first directors with full names, addresses, and consent to act; (e) registered office address in Alberta; and (f) business restrictions (none applicable to digital game publishing). Submit the electronic articles, attest as incorporator, and remit the CAD 100.00 statutory filing fee through the provincial secure payment gateway.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as First Director (Form 2) for each first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a Deficiency Notice identifying outstanding fields, the filer has 30 days to amend and resubmit. Rejected filings are eligible for partial refund after 90 days; expedited re-filing may be effected on the same business day via the online portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Kit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Corporate Registry e-Filing System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the Alberta incorporation number and the official corporate seal identifier. Initiate the statutory minute book containing the by-laws, share ledger, blank share certificates, and certified copy of the Articles. Record the registered office and confirm that no physical counterpart of the certificate is required in Alberta.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate is delayed or contains clerical errors, apply to the Corporate Registry for a correction certificate under ABCA s. 13(7) within 30 days at no additional state fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inaugural Board Meeting and First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (internal governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold an organizational meeting or circulate a unanimous written consent adopting the by-laws, approving the pro-forma First Board Resolution, electing officers, fixing the registered office, and authorizing the opening of bank and payment settlement accounts (Steam/Valve payout and PlayStation Store payout) and engagement of legal and tax advisors. Issue share certificates to the founding shareholders and record all proceedings in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Form 4 Notice of Directors (if any change occurs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director consent or officer appointment deficiency is identified, adopt a ratifying board resolution and file the corresponding Notice of Change of Directors with the Corporate Registry to cure the omission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online; Alberta Revenue – Corporate Tax Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the electronic business registration with the CRA Business Registration Online portal to obtain a nine-digit Business Number (BN), including GST/HST registration where taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 and any payroll deduction program accounts. Concurrently register the Corporation with Alberta Revenue for provincial corporate income tax under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act, using the BN as the provincial account identifier. Obtain CRA My Business Account access codes.
required_dossiers: Officer identification and CRA authorization forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA rejects the BN application, call CRA Business Enquiries (1-800-959-5525) within 15 days and supply any missing officer identification. If Alberta Revenue shows no account, re-file through the Corporate Registry connection to CORES and confirm the BN-linked Alberta corporate tax account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business License and Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary – Business Licensing and Permitting & Inspections Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a City of Calgary Business Licence under the commercial office/digital services classification, attaching the lease, zoning verification, and a statement of digital software publishing activity. Confirm premises compliance with the Alberta Building Code occupancy requirements and obtain a fire safety clearance from the Calgary Fire Department for the occupied floor area, if a commercial office is used.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and CRA Business Number
Registered office lease and landlord consent
Calgary Fire Department safety inspection certificate (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the City queries zoning or licence classification, amend the application, submit a Zoning Compliance Letter from the Calgary Planning Portal, and pay only the incremental inspection fee rather than a duplicate licence fee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: City of Calgary Business Licensing Authority (municipal operating permit) and Service Alberta Corporate Registry (registered office and corporate records); no federal broadcast, radio-spectrum, or content-licensing permit applies to Internet-only Steam and PlayStation Store publishing channels.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: City of Calgary Business Licence – Commercial Digital Publishing and Online Software Distribution (Business Operating Licence; provincial video game tax credit registration, if claimed, is a fiscal registration and not a permit).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Protected Areas (EPA), Government of Alberta – Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, Activities Designation Regulation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is classified as Schedule 1 exclusion for information-technology and office use; no EIA registration or approval is required for cloud-based software publishing premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated wastewater, VOC, or particulate discharge thresholds apply to pure digital distribution; compliance obligations are limited to municipal storm-sewer by-law compliance, electronic waste disposal through an Alberta Recycling Management Authority approved collector, and refrigerant handling under the Alberta Ozone Protection Regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Calgary Fire Department annual fire safety inspection certificate covering egress capacity, extinguisher placement, and emergency lighting; Alberta Municipal Affairs structural load and occupancy approval for the registered office floor; Alberta OHS Code (AR 87/2009) Parts 2 and 11 workplace clearance covering emergency preparedness, workspace ventilation, first aid, WHMIS orientation, and injury reporting records for information-technology employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — administered through the CRA 'My Business Account' portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html) and Business Registration Online (BRO); provincial registry counterpart: Alberta Corporate Registry / Alberta Registries.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Canadian-resident ULC: (1) incorporate under the Alberta Business Corporations Act and obtain the Alberta Corporate Access Number; (2) apply to CRA for the nine-digit federal Business Number (BN) via Business Registration Online (BRO), Form RC1, or telephone; the GST/HST (RT) program account is issued simultaneously, while the corporate income tax (RC) account is opened automatically upon incorporation; (3) where foreign shareholders exist, file Form RC372 for the non-resident account and the first T2 corporate return in the ULC's initial taxation year; (4) register for GST/HST under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act when making taxable supplies in Canada and when the 'small supplier' exemption (C$30,000 threshold) is exceeded; since 1 July 2021, a non-resident digital platform or supplier must also consider the simplified (STAR) registration regime for supplies of digital services to Canadian consumers; (5) open a CRA payroll (RP) account only if Canadian employees are engaged.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — notwithstanding this hybrid classification, the Alberta ULC is an entity-level taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act (Canada) on worldwide income; pass-through features arise through: (i) the subsection 39(11) election allowing non-resident shareholders to treat ULC shares as partnership interests on disposition; (ii) US 'check-the-box' transparency for US shareholders; and (iii) unlimited shareholder liability, which enables treaty-based flow-through claims in certain cross-border contexts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (a) Income Tax Act subsection 39(11) election — ULC shares deemed partnership interests for computing non-resident shareholders' gains and losses on disposition; (b) ITA section 216 election for net-rental income of non-resident owners; (c) Excise Tax Act section 156 election (Form GST25) to deem supplies among closely related corporations to be made for nil consideration; (d) ETA section 211.1 election for non-resident registrants; (e) US Form 8832 'check-the-box' classification election affecting the home-jurisdiction characterisation of the Canadian ULC; (f) capital cost allowance class elections at the corporate level.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonised Sales Tax) — federal value-added tax under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; Alberta applies no provincial sales tax, so only the 5% federal GST is chargeable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 — measured on total worldwide taxable supplies in the current calendar quarter and the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters ('small supplier' threshold under ETA s.148); digital platform operators and non-resident suppliers of digital services to Canadian consumers apply the same C$30,000 threshold under the modified July 2021 regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None — Canada does not impose mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, digital stamping, or API-based e-invoicing. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically (GST/HST NETFILE) when annual taxable turnover exceeds C$1.5M; the voluntary Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework (PEPPOL BIS 3.0 / Business Payments in Canada) is available; zero-rated export records must be retained for six years from the end of the taxation year in either paper or electronic format.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to a taxable supply of intangible personal property (e.g., PC/console game licences and Steam/PlayStation digital content) made by a GST/HST registrant to a non-resident person not registered under Part IX of the ETA, provided the supply is for the non-resident's consumption or use outside Canada (ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s.25.1). For an individual purchaser, the ordinary country of residence governs; for a corporate purchaser, the jurisdiction where the corporation is resident or has a fixed establishment governs under the s.26.1 place-of-supply rules. Revenue routed through the Canadian ULC from foreign platform payout rails (Steam Valve, PlayStation Store) is zero-rated where the platform is the non-resident recipient and the underlying customers are non-resident; contemporaneous documentation must evidence the foreign destination and the purchaser's non-resident status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Customs Export Declaration (B13A or CADEX electronic filing) — applicable only where physical encoded media or server-hosting hardware crosses the border; not required for cloud or digital delivery
Commercial invoice or digital sale contract containing foreign purchaser identifiers, place-of-supply attestation, and payment terms
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (physical-media distribution only)
Steam Valve / PlayStation Store payout statements evidencing foreign-platform settlement and foreign customer jurisdictions
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the Canadian deposit-taking institution for FX conversions above regulatory reporting thresholds
Transfer-pricing documentation (OECD Chapter V / CRA policy) demonstrating arm's-length consideration for the publishing intangibles
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA will disallow zero-rating and reassess uncollected GST/HST at 5% (plus any applicable provincial component) where the exporter cannot substantiate that the digital supply was made to a non-resident and consumed outside Canada. The normal reassessment period is 4 years for corporations (3 years for individuals), extending to 7 years or indefinitely for misrepresentation, neglect, or non-arm's length transactions. Penalties: 50% gross-negligence penalty under ITA s.163(2) / ETA s.285 of the understated tax; C$100 to C$25,000 per instance for false statements and omissions (ETA s.280); criminal prosecution under ITA s.239 / ETA s.327 carries fines of up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years. Interest at the prescribed rate compounds daily from the original filing due date. Reassessment clawback is retrospective with no forgiveness window for fraudulent export zero-rating claims; transfer-pricing penalties (ITA s.247(3)) add 10% of the net adjustment. Canada imposes no specific statutory FX repatriation deadline for zero-rated exports; the 180-day convention reflects standard Canadian export-credit terms and CRA transfer-pricing expectations for foreign receivables, beyond which documentation of continued foreign use is required.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Department of Finance Canada. Canada has no standalone foreign-exchange control agency; the Bank of Canada is the monetary authority and the future registrar for the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) payment service provider framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility as an IMF Article VIII member. The Canadian dollar (CAD) floats freely and there are no exchange controls restricting capital inflows, outflows, dividend remittances, or royalty distributions for Alberta ULCs. The only cross-border impediments are tax-driven, namely Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (generally 25% for non-treaty beneficiaries, often reduced by treaty, with Canada-US treaty rates typically 15% on dividends and 0-10% on royalties). No convertibility approval is required for digital gaming revenue repatriated from Steam or PlayStation storefronts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender obligation, no statutory conversion timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio exists in Canada. Export receipts from video game publishing may be retained in CAD, USD, EUR, or any foreign currency indefinitely. Reporting obligations that apply are (i) FINTRAC record-keeping and reporting for transactions at or above CAD $10,000 or the equivalent in foreign currency, and (ii) Statistics Canada trade-in-services reporting, but neither requires repatriation or FX conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for Cross-Border US Payouts

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with legal constraints. Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) can be used for multi-currency collections from Steam, PlayStation, and other platforms, but under Canada's Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) and Retail Payment Activities Regulations (in force September 2024), any payment service provider serving Canadian entities must register with the Bank of Canada and maintain a Canadian presence. The EMI must also be a registered money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC. Foreign EMIs cannot access LVTS ACSS settlement rails and do not offer true Schedule I Canadian bank guarantees. Legal constraint: reliance on an unregistered offshore EMI may create AML/KYC deficiencies at the tier-1 bank. Recommended posture: EMI as secondary collection-wallet, tier-1 bank as primary treasury spine.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is generally permitted for Alberta ULCs with tier-1 Canadian banks, provided that directors complete FINTRAC-JVIT-compliant video identity verification and that the ULC files an Alberta corporate registry extract showing a registered office and, for non-resident directors, a notarized power of attorney and Canadian agent for service. Several banks, including ATB Financial and CIBC, escalate non-resident-owned ULC files to enhanced due diligence and may mandate one physical sign-off at an Alberta branch; this is a practical requirement rather than a statutory one. Onboarding timeline typically ranges from two to four weeks for a standard gaming-publishing ULC without regulatory license requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or beneficial owner creating beneficial-ownership opacity for the ULC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports of directors and 25%-plus shareholders; six-month proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement); source-of-wealth narrative and corroborating financial statements for share subscription; Canada Revenue Agency corporate tax account letter; Alberta Notice of Articles and certificate of status; executed unanimous shareholder agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid high-volume storefront payouts from Steam and PlayStation without an established operating history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Valve Steamworks Publishing Agreement and Sony PlayStation Partner Agreement; Steamworks partner portal analytics report; PlayStation partner revenue reports; 12-month projected net revenue schedule; royalty payment reconciliation spreadsheet; storefront sales tax exemption certificates if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC unlimited-liability structure classified as high-risk or unusual by the bank's financial-crime unit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Notice of Articles confirming ULC status; unanimous shareholder agreement describing unlimited liability allocation; solvency opinion or comfort letter from a licensed CPA; board resolution confirming no shareholder personal liability exposure beyond corporate obligations; franchise or business plan demonstrating commercial legitimacy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire screening flags generated by payments from mixed foreign jurisdictions or platform marketplaces
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete platform registration certificate showing permitted storefront territories; platform-level sanctions-assurance letter; list of all distribution jurisdictions with expected revenue volumes; bank-standard end-user undertaking and sanctions questionnaire; regular export-of-goods-and-services reporting to Statistics Canada.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a foreign fintech EMI as settlement intermediary triggering suspicion of money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EMI FINTRAC MSB registration number; Bank of Canada RPAA PSP registration certificate; wire audit trail mapping all inbound EMI transactions to beneficiary ULC accounts; signed agreements with each EMI; detailed ledger entries matching platform net revenue statements to bank deposits.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Preferred rail is SWIFT MT103 for non-USD jurisdictions and ABA/Fedwire routing for USD originating in the United States. Payment purpose code: equity injection or subscription for shares, identified on MT103 field 70 as EQUITY CONTRIBUTION CA_ULC SHARE SUBSCRIPTION. For USD injections, instruct the remitting US bank to use the Canadian bank's US clearing subsidiary (e.g., BMO Harris Bank, TD Bank N.A., CIBC U.S.) to avoid double FX conversion and to preserve audit visibility. Supporting verification package: executed share subscription agreement; board resolution authorizing issuance of shares; Alberta corporate registry confirmation; CRA tax account evidence; and a cleared counterparty list for the onboarding bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic CAD disbursements: use the LVTS (Large Value Transfer System) for high-value settlements and ACSS for batch daily clearing. Cross-border trade settlements for royalties, middleware vendor fees, engine licenses, and localization costs: SWIFT MT103 with ISO 20022 purpose codes such as ROY (royalties and license fees) routed via Fedwire or CHIPS through the bank's US correspondent. Commercial letters of credit (MT700) are structurally unsuited to digital Steam and PlayStation royalty flows; the recommended instrument set is platform-operator irrevocable payment undertakings plus MT103 telegraphic transfers into dedicated USD and CAD clear accounts. Maintain separate USD clear account and CAD operational account to minimize conversion spreads and to align with Valve's and Sony's payout remittance cycles.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright CAD/USD deliverable forward contracts with maturity up to 12 months offered by tier-1 Canadian bank dealing desks
Cash-settled non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CAD executed with non-resident banks or global dealers where the Canadian bank credit line constrains deliverable forward access
Cross-currency CAD/USD swap agreements for operational liquidity hedging of recurring Steam and PlayStation net revenue flows
CAD/USD foreign-exchange option collars (zero-premium risk reversals) structured as low-risk hedging for uneven platform payout timing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (online fee CAD 20 / paper fee CAD 45; corporate registry anniversary filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 (approx. USD 74) late filing penalty after the 60-day window; failure to file for two consecutive anniversaries triggers administrative strike-off; revival requires Court-ordered reinstatement and additional fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporate Income Tax Return (T2), including Alberta corporate tax schedules and ULC additional information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end -> due June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (maximum 12 months); repeated non-filing may lead to CRA default assessments, garnishment, prosecution, and director liability; T2 instalments required when tax owing exceeds CAD 3,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Return (mandatory once annual taxable Canadian revenue exceeds CAD 30,000; Steam/PlayStation digital sales to Canadian consumers are taxable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers (revenue under CAD 500,000): within 3 months after fiscal year-end; quarterly filers (revenue over CAD 500,000): within 1 month after calendar quarter-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of balance owing plus 1% per full month late, plus compound arrears interest at the CRA prescribed rate; chronic non-filing may lead to registration cancellation and gross-negligence penalties up to 25%.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T106 Information Return (non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents; required for royalty or platform-payout arrangements with US parent/affiliates)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the same date as the T2 return (no extension available): six months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 25 per day per non-resident contract (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500), plus transfer-pricing reassessments; misrepresentation penalty of 10% to 25% where the net transfer-pricing adjustment exceeds CAD 5 million.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA) s. 152(2), a private (non-distributing) ULC is exempt from appointing an auditor for the fiscal year if all shareholders pass a unanimous consent resolution; a distributing corporation can never waive the audit. No statutory revenue or asset threshold exists; any shareholder holding 5% or more of the issued shares may demand an audit (ABCA s. 151(4)). Lenders and Steam/PlayStation publisher agreements frequently require an audit or independent review engagement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook – IFRS applies to publicly accountable enterprises; a private Alberta ULC may elect either IFRS or ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises). The CRA T2 return requires taxable income to be reconciled from accounting income via Schedule 1.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Alberta ABCA (as amended by the Business Corporations Amendment Act, 2020) requires the ULC to maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC). The ISC register must be updated within 15 days of any share transfer or change in significant control and kept at the registered office; no annual filing of the ISC register is made to Service Alberta, but it must be produced on lawful demand by the Corporate Registry or a law-enforcement agency. The annual T2 return (Schedule 50) discloses all shareholders and non-resident ownership to the CRA, and a US-parent ULC must report its check-the-box election status to the CRA on Form RC4651.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 110–590 (CAD 150–800) per annum for a commercial registered agent in Calgary or Edmonton; self-managed office at the ULC's Canadian physical address is permitted under the ABCA
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000–32,000 (CAD 11,000–43,000) for a full statutory audit of a mid-size game publisher; USD 3,500–8,000 for a review engagement; USD 1,500–4,000 for a compilation-only CRA-ready financial package

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined federal-provincial general corporate rate (15% federal Part I + 8% Alberta provincial). Where the ULC qualifies as a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC), the Small Business Deduction applies at 11% combined (9% federal + 2% Alberta) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; however, a ULC held by US non-residents is generally not CCPC-eligible and is taxed at 23%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit: 35% fully refundable on qualifying current expenditures for CCPCs within specified income limits, otherwise 15% non-refundable ITC. Alberta currently provides no digital-media or video-game-specific corporate tax credit; arm's-length royalty and platform-commission expenses paid to Valve, Sony, and rights holders remain deductible. The non-capital loss regime provides the principal timing benefit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) incorporating Schedule 5 (Alberta corporate tax computation); mandatory electronic filing via CRA E-file through approved third-party software or the CRA Forms portal. Alberta provincial corporate income tax is administered by the CRA under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act and filed jointly with the T2; no separate provincial paper return exists.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 must be filed within 6 months of the taxation year-end (e.g., fiscal year ended 31 December 2025 is due 30 June 2026). Final balance of federal and Alberta corporate tax is payable by 2 months after year-end for non-CCPCs and 3 months for qualifying CCPCs; quarterly or monthly instalments are required when prior-year tax exceeds CAD 3,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, CRA business number (BN/RT), jurisdiction of incorporation (Alberta), mailing and registered office address, fiscal period end, and industry classification code (NAICS 511210 / ISIC 5820).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select entity status as 'Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC)'; provide Alberta articles number; a non-resident director may serve but the registered office and records must remain accessible to the CRA in Alberta.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from PC/console video game publishing, Steam/PlayStation Store sales, downloadable content, microtransactions, subscriptions, and licensing, net of refunds, chargebacks, and platform commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize platform payouts on a gross basis with commissions treated as selling and distribution expenses; intercompany revenue from the US parent must satisfy the arm's-length standard under s.247 I.T.A.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income per financial statements adjusted under Part I I.T.A.: add back non-deductible club dues, penalties, and excessive entertainment costs; deduct capital cost allowance (Schedule 1), eligible SR&ED expenditures (Schedule 31), and residual non-capital losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only arm's-length royalty, development, and marketing fees paid to related non-resident service providers; keep contemporaneous OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation to sustain deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax at 15% general rate on taxable income, or 9% for the portion eligible for the small business deduction where ULC is CCPC-qualified.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A US-shareholder-owned ULC is typically a non-CCPC; claim no federal small business deduction and apply the 15% general rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Lines 360 to 500 - Credits and Federal Balance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct investment tax credits (Schedule 8), foreign tax credits (Schedule 21), and general tax reductions to arrive at net federal Part I balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the US shareholder treats the ULC as fiscally transparent, US taxes paid at the shareholder level are creditable in the United States, not in Canada; no Canadian foreign tax credit should be claimed on flow-through income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial taxable income computation and allocation to Alberta; apply 8% general rate (2% Alberta small business rate for CCPC-eligible ULCs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Absent a permanent establishment outside Alberta, allocate 100% of taxable income to Alberta; an exclusively digital sales footprint with a registered Alberta office does not create foreign PE exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 9 / Part XIII - Non-Resident Withholding Summary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate dividends, royalties, interest, and rentals paid or credited to non-resident persons in the tax year, with Part XIII tax withheld and remitted on NR4 forms.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record each ULC dividend paid to the US shareholder with treaty-reduced rates supported by Form 6166 and Form NR301; royalty rates for software copyrights may qualify for 0% relief under Article XII of the Canada-US Treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form T106 - Non-Arm's Length Transactions Summary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full disclosure of every reportable cross-border non-arm's length transaction with related persons, including royalty payments, development fees, marketing cost-sharing, and loan balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when the aggregate annual value of applicable transactions exceeds CAD 1 million, or intercompany loans exceed CAD 1 million at any time; attach T106-1 to T106-4 detail schedules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months (maximum 17%); for a second failure within three years, 10% plus 2% per month up to 24 months (maximum 38%). Late or insufficient instalment interest accrues daily at the CRA prescribed rate (approximately 8% per annum for 2025), compounded daily. Failure to file T106: CAD 100 per day for first 40 days, CAD 2,500 minimum to CAD 25,000 maximum depending on category; gross negligence under s.163(2) adds 50% of the understated tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act on dividends paid or credited by a resident Canadian corporation to a non-resident shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For a US-resident shareholder of the Alberta ULC, invoke the Canada-US Tax Treaty: (i) the shareholder obtains IRS Form 6166 (Certificate of US Residency for tax treaty purposes); (ii) the shareholder completes and delivers CRA Form NR301 (Request for Treaty-Based Reduction of Foreign Non-Resident Tax Withholding) to the ULC as withholding agent; (iii) the ULC applies the treaty-reduced rate of 5% where the beneficial owner is a US corporation owning at least 10% of the ULC's voting stock, or 15% in all other cases; (iv) the ULC remits Part XIII tax to the CRA and files NR4 slips. If the ULC is treated as fiscally transparent in the United States, Treaty Article IV(7) permits the shareholder to claim treaty benefits on the underlying Canadian-source payment, and the ULC may file a Form NR7 refund claim for excess withheld amounts.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 25% Part XIII; Canada-US Treaty Article XI reduces to 0% for arm's-length interest and 15% for non-arm's-length interest. Software and video-game copyright royalties: statutory 25%; Treaty Article XII grants a 0% source-country rate for royalties on computer software and copyrighted video-game content. Patent and trademark royalties: statutory 25%; Treaty rate 10% for US residents. All royalty and interest claims require Form NR301 and beneficial-ownership documentation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: T106 mandatory where aggregate annual non-arm's length cross-border transactions with non-residents exceed CAD 1,000,000, or where intercompany loans/advances exceed CAD 1,000,000 in carrying value at any point in the year. Local File and Master File compliance under CRA Information Circular IC 87-2R and OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines triggers when the Canadian taxpayer's gross revenue exceeds CAD 50 million, or the multinational group's assets exceed CAD 50 million; Country-by-Country Report (Form RC4649) required for groups with consolidated revenue of at least CAD 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada operates no EP-based Economic Substance Regulation equivalent to the UAE or Cayman regimes; however, substance is enforced through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s.245 I.T.A.), the transfer-pricing recharacterization rule (s.247(2) I.T.A.), treaty beneficial-ownership and Limitation-on-Benefits provisions under Canada-US Treaty Article XXIX A, and BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch rules. The Alberta ULC must show real decision-making, operational staff, physical premises, and risk-bearing capital in Alberta; purely passive mailbox ULCs are disregarded by the CRA on audit. The ULC's inherent unlimited liability under the Alberta Business Corporations Act s.15(1)-(2) provides a strong commercial substance indicator, and GST/HST registration and Canadian payroll demonstrate further residency and substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting Steam or PlayStation Store revenue, fabricating platform commission deductions, issuing false intercompany invoices to the US parent, or maintaining undisclosed foreign bank accounts for publishing payouts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under s.239(1) I.T.A.: fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded plus imprisonment for up to 5 years, or both; civil gross-negligence penalty under s.163(2) I.T.A.: 50% of the understated federal and provincial tax; the CRA Criminal Investigations Program may impose restraint orders on all corporate and personal assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: All directors and officers who participated in the fraudulent scheme face joint and several criminal liability; s.227.1 I.T.A. imposes civil joint and several liability for unremitted amounts; as a ULC, shareholders are personally liable for the corporation's debts under ABCA s.15(2), allowing the CRA and creditors to pierce the corporate veil without court application.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unpaid Part XIII Withholding on Dividends, Royalties, and Interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits to US shareholders without deducting the statutory 25% Part XIII tax, or claiming 5%/0% treaty rates without a valid Form 6166 and Form NR301 on file; failing to remit withheld amounts within the statutory deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to withhold or remit is subject to a 10% penalty under s.227(8) I.T.A., daily compound interest on the arrears, and immediate demand for the full unremitted amount; the CRA may issue a s.225.2 jeopardy order freezing bank accounts and garnishing Steam/PlayStation payouts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally and severally liable for the entire unremitted Part XIII tax plus interest and penalties under s.227.1(1) I.T.A.; CRA issues director liability letters directly to US-resident directors without requiring a Canadian collection judgment; unpaid director liability can trigger cross-border enforcement and travel restrictions under reciprocal US-Canada tax collection agreements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Shell Abuse (GAAR)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing development fees, IP licensing, or marketing support through the ULC at non-arm's-length prices to shift Canadian taxable profit to no-tax or low-tax affiliates; employing the US check-the-box hybrid status of the ULC to create a double-dip deduction inconsistent with BEPS Action 2; or operating the ULC as a shell with no Canadian employees, office, or risk-bearing functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: s.247(2) I.T.A. permits the CRA to recharacterize or adjust the transaction to an arm's-length amount; s.247(3) imposes a 10% transfer-pricing penalty on the adjustment (minimum CAD 5,000); s.245 I.T.A. GAAR denies deductions where the transaction lacks bona fide substance; failure to file T106 attracts daily penalties and an additional 50% gross-negligence penalty under s.163(2) for deficient documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the intercompany pricing are subject to s.227.1 for associated withholding deficiencies; in a GAAR or sham finding, the unlimited liability nature of the ULC renders shareholders personally liable for the tax deficiency and professional fees; additionally, CRA may use s.160 I.T.A. to assess transferee liability against shareholders who received diverted corporate assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directing Steam Payouts or PlayStation Store remittances to a personal account, an offshore shell, or a foreign payment intermediary without recording the ULC as the beneficial owner; structuring cash or crypto transactions to evade the CAD 10,000 reporting threshold; failing to maintain beneficial-ownership records for the ULC's issued shares.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 for a corporate entity under s.73 of the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; failure to register as a money services business where the ULC converts digital-store proceeds or performs currency exchange carries a fine and 5 years' imprisonment; the CRA may reallocate the diverted income to the controlling shareholder and apply a 50% negligence penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers face criminal liability under Criminal Code s.462.31 for laundering proceeds of designated offences; FINTRAC can impose separate AMLs of up to CAD 500,000 on individual directors who direct payment-rail diversion; the Alberta ULC's unlimited liability regime additionally exposes every shareholder to third-party restitution claims, civil forfeiture, and prohibition from serving as a director of any Canadian corporation for up to 10 years.
